page: Amazon Web Services r4.2xlarge is a legacy fourth-generation memory-optimized virtual machine hosted on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. The instance is configured with 8 virtual CPUs across 4 dedicated physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, alongside 45 MB of shared L3 cache. It delivers 61.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 7.62 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not feature onboard local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators such as GPUs, and network connectivity is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate typical characteristics of an older CPU generation. In raw compute tests, the system yields weak to poor relative throughput, as shown by a single-core stress-ng metric of 883.89 and a multi-core score of 4154.8, along with a Geekbench multi-core score of 3333.0. Instruction set extensions include baseline AVX and cryptographic AES capabilities, but lack newer vector instructions like AVX-512 or AMX. Memory performance is mixed; while 256 MB uncached read bandwidth reaches an average 41.57 GB/sec and the PassMark memory score sits at an average 2184.03, write throughput and small-block cached transfers remain in the lower percentiles. Application testing registers 2.32 million Redis SET operations per second and 5.36 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Cost efficiency for the r4.2xlarge is primarily dictated by its legacy status and high memory-to-vCPU ratio. While modern architectures offer superior per-core performance and instructions-per-clock efficiency, this configuration retains value where capacity demands outweigh processing power. With no bundled local storage, persistent disk operations rely entirely on attached network volumes. The instance is primarily suited for memory-intensive caching tiers, intermediate relational database deployments, in-memory processing, and legacy enterprise software requiring substantial RAM allocation without demanding modern compute throughput.
description: Amazon Web Services r4.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the Xen hypervisor, powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor with 8 vCPUs (4 physical cores) clocked at 2.3 GHz and 61.0 GB of RAM. The instance lacks integrated GPUs and local storage, relying on network-attached storage and providing a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Across benchmark evaluations, the legacy CPU architecture yields weak compute and single-core metrics, including a Geekbench single-core score of 880.0 and multi-core score of 3333.0, though it maintains stable uncached memory read bandwidth of 41.57 GB/sec. Because its compute performance per core is limited relative to newer platforms, the configuration is best aligned with memory-bound workloads where processing demands are modest, such as Redis caching clusters, medium-scale in-memory databases, and memory-heavy enterprise backend services.
